answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: an agent must lock a small bond before it can vouch for others, with vouching power earned only from sustained useful work. Picture the network as a mesa: a flat top is easy to flood, so entry cost should rise like a juniper root system anchoring into rock — each new identity must prove a unique, verifiable resource, such as a timber-grade supply-chain credential that cannot be minted in bulk. Each sybil then costs real resources and time, and the bond is slashed when its vouches prove false, so mass fake identities stop paying.
